name: Branch Lines, Condensed
tagline: Branch Lines re-set as one IBM Plex superfamily: the signal box's legends, stamps and keys engraved in Plex Sans Condensed, the family's words in Plex Sans, one dotted zero in every figure, and every lamp, ring and prompt hung outside the text edge.
concept: This is Branch Lines with only its type re-set, as one IBM Plex superfamily in which width sets the hierarchy. Everything engraved on the signal box's panel is set in Plex Sans Condensed: titles, heads, labels, the timetables' stamps, counts, the keys and the bar. Everything the family keeps and says is in Plex Sans, Plex Mono prints only the machine's own name and the small print, and the tubes stay VT323. Zero is dotted everywhere, and every lamp, ring and prompt hangs outside the edge of the words. It should feel like the same calm signal box at night, with its legends engraved in one engineering hand.
companions: Unchanged from the parent, as the roll requires. Steel-cyan #a7c4d8 is the family's hand and the wiring: rails, rings, links and the backlit steel key for 'here'. The boards and plates are green-black slate. Section and kind colours appear only in rings and lamps. Amber means late or needs a look and nothing else. #6dff9c lights only what is now and live: the mark, 'next', Send, the box, the now lamps and the runs from them, her screens and the tubes.
decisions: Choice of face. The dice offered three condensed faces and I took IBM Plex Sans Condensed. Barlow Condensed is the highway-sign face the panel marked down as sporty 'trail-sign' heads in round 6, and it has no stylistic sets. Archivo narrow was already the parent's title face at 84%, its 400 body looked pale in round 12, and it has no stylistic sets either. Plex Condensed forms one superfamily with Plex Sans and Plex Mono; 'condensed Plex heads over Plex body' was rewarded in rounds 6, 8 and 12. It is IBM's own face for an IBM-green screen, and it carries the sets the third roll needs.

The system: width sets the hierarchy. The condensed face is for what is engraved on the panel: page titles, section heads, the 14px label step, stamps and relative days, counts and figures, the chat's speaker names and times, field labels, the bar, tabs, keys and buttons. Plex Sans is for what the family keeps and says: row names, Vera's and the family's words, ledes, help text, fields, the select's words and the ways to start. Plex Mono sets only the wordmark, the footer's small print and code. VT323 is unchanged on the glass.

The stamps left the typewriter. Every date, time and relative day that the parent set in DM Mono is now a condensed legend. Plex's digits are tabular by default, so the timetable margins, the chat's spine, To do's Due column and the Drive column still read straight down. This answers round 13's note that whole phrases in letterspaced mono were not rewarded, and the revival judge's request to set the date kicker condensed.

A written scale. Titles are 48.8px at weight 600 and -0.008em; heads 24px at 600; legends 14px at 500 and +0.01em. The keys and the bar are 16px condensed at 500, with 600 on the primary. Body text is Plex Sans 16/1.6 at 400, with row names at 600, and small text is 14px. Figures: the page figure is 400 in the label's steel, the fortnight's day numerals are 34px at 600, and the tally is 42px at 600. I cut the heads' word-spacing from .08em to .03em, because Plex Condensed's space is already open. The smallest words rise from 11.52px to 12px, and the phone fortnight's 'in 4 days' from 11.5px to 13px.

Home's question is the page's title, so it is set at the title step in the condensed face: clamp(1.875rem, 4.4vw, 3.05rem). That is 48.8px on the desktop and 30px on a phone. At 34px it broke onto two lines on the phone, so I lowered the floor until it held one line. It is still the box's label.

The stylistic set is ss04, Plex's dotted zero, in the Sans and the Condensed. Plex Mono draws the same zero by default, so zero is drawn one way on the whole page off the glass; the lineage was faulted before for drawing it two ways. I left ss01 and ss02 (the simple a and g) off, because in round 10 the panel found Plex's schoolbook a and g soft. Every font shorthand resets the features, so the set is held at * with !important, and the mono elements get their own zero back.

Hung by hand. On the Next up tube the '>' prompt hangs in the glass's margin, so '4 more on the radar' starts at the title's edge. The rings in Lately added and the kids' wishes now sit under the head's icon, with the names on the head's own text edge; they had been 4.8px in. Status's bands are aligned the same way. The Ideas and Settings lists' names start at the page title's edge, with their rings and icons hanging to its left; they had been 3-4px in. Coming up's note starts where the head's words start. The numbered steps and the tips list on the settings pages hang their numerals and bullets outside the paragraph. To do's column heads now sit over their columns; Who had been 2px off.

One markup change. The drive macro in ideas.html pads the minutes to two digits ('2 h 05 min'), so the Drive column's tabular figures line up, as the type judge asked. On the glass, .rel now inherits the tube's VT323, so the Ideas tube's '18 min NW' is in the tube's own lettering again. In the parent it had fallen into DM Mono.

Nothing else changed: the colours, the light, the layout, the lines and the words are all the parent's. The sources are the parent's files, re-set by src/retype.py (each replacement must match exactly once), plus src/type.css. src/build.py builds them into 58.4K of the 60K budget.
title: What’s *next* for us? These are the parent's words, which a dice mutant keeps; they are now set at the title step in the condensed face, 48.8px on desktop and one line at 30px on a phone. It says FamilyDB's job in the family's own 'us': deciding the weekend, the next outing or the next thing to get done. 'next' is also the diagram's own meaning of the lit green: now, and what comes next down the line.
measures: ink_on_bg is 12.75 and brand_on_bg 15.18, both the parent's. Green share: Home 79.7%, Ideas 84.8%, Chat 97.3%, Status 99.1%. Hue entropy: Home .38, Ideas .35, Chat .29, Status .25. 0 of Home's 57 targets are under 44px, and 0 on every other rendered page, desktop and phone. The smallest words are 12px (11.97px for the code in General's help), up from 11.52px. Nothing scrolls sideways. Contrast and colour-separation checks are unchanged and all pass. The css is 58,403 of 60,000 characters. The full render has 0 hard failures and one guideline flag, Ideas' words 28.3% different from today's, which is inherited from the parent. Against the parent, 3-9% of pixels differ per page (Home 8.3%, Chat 4.2%, Ideas 4.8%, Status 2.7%).
strengths: One rule holds on every page, Plans, To do and Settings included: the panel's legends are condensed and the family's words are in the text face. The change reaches every line of every page.
The timetables read as engraved legends rather than typewriter phrases. Every figure is tabular, so the margins, the Drive column ('2 h 05 min') and Status's tables line up without a monospace.
Zero is drawn one way, dotted, across the page, which gives the figures a quiet machine texture (10:00, $0.00, 30 September).
The question is now the largest head on Home, at the title step, and it holds one line on a phone.
Markers hang: each list's names start at its head's words or the page title's edge, with rings, lamps and the tube's prompt in the margin.
No target is under 44px on any rendered page, nothing scrolls sideways, and the smallest words are 12px (up from 11.52px).
weaknesses: It is a type mutant: only 3-9% of pixels differ from the parent (Home 8.3%, Chat 4.2%, Status 2.7%). At half size it reads as Branch Lines, and the parent's colour faults carry over unchanged (Chat 97% and Status 99% green by share).
Plex has only tabular figures, so in running text a 1 takes a whole figure's width with its slab foot. '$1.26' and '10:00' look gappy in prose.
The dotted zero also reaches Vera's own words ('10:00 to 14:00'), where some will find it fussy or machine-like.
The set is held with a universal !important, the blunt tool the round-13 type judge disliked.
The condensed face and the text face are one design, so a legend differs from a row in width, not in voice. DM Sans's round warmth is gone, and Plex SemiBold row names are denser.
Checkbox labels that are whole sentences read tight in the condensed face, for example Memory's 'A must or a never (an allergy, a rule), not only a taste'.

The quotes half of the roll had nothing to hang. No rendered page starts a line with a quotation mark; the only quotes sit mid-line on Status and Memory. So no rule for quotes was written, and the bullets carry the roll alone.
The tube's hung prompt sits about 5px from the glass's edge. Plex Sans Condensed is served as static weights, so the parent's 650-weight heads became 600.

name: Night Departures, Surveyed
tagline: Night Departures drawn up as the railway engineer's survey: under each green screen a steel scale measures what it shows (the days to each departure, the minutes to each place, the dollars against the day's limit), every page and section wears a drawn emblem hung on its rule, the setup steps are numbered balloons, and each kind of idea wears a small ringed badge in its own colour.
concept: Night Departures with only its pictures redrawn in one draughtsman's hand: the station after dark becomes the engineer's survey of the line. Each green screen keeps its phosphor, and under it a thin steel scale measures what the screen shows as a picture. Each section of the house is drawn as a part on a drawing: a detail circle, an axis, one dimension or one callout. The feel is calm and precise, a blueprint pinned beside the departure board. The only new light is NOW, the lamp at each scale's datum.
companions: No colour changed. Every token is the parent's: #6dff9c on #0b0f0d, steel rails, the enamel line colours, copper for the family, wayfinding-yellow links, amber for late. The new drawings add two steels that are only line weights, not companions: a draughtsman's hairline (#6d808b) for frames, leaders, extension lines and centre lines, and a lighter steel (#8fa3ae) for dimension lines, arrowheads and major ticks. Colour inside the drawings follows the parent's code. Emblem pictograms take the page's line colour (lilac for Ideas, sky for Plans, teal for To do, pink for Wishes) or steel on a facility. Kind badges take the kind's colour for the ring, a 10-14% tint and the drawing (warm kinds held to 10%). Plan stops on Home's scale are sky, place ticks on the Ideas scale lilac. Amber marks only the step you are at in the setup balloons and the 75% mark where the spend screen turns amber. The only new green is the NOW lamp at the datum of each weeks scale.
decisions: MAJOR, schematic language, monitors. A scale under each screen, and each carries data, not dimensions of the case. Round 10's 'Programme Guide, Drafted' lost for '80 COL / 25 LN' costume, so none of that here. Home's departure board gets a four-week scale: weekends hatched, each coming plan a stop labelled with its day ('Thu 1', 'Sun 4', 'Sat 17'), the next one filled. Its one dimension reads '5 plans in 24 days', so the gaps between plans and the free weekends show at a glance. The Ideas map gets its rings laid out along a line (home, 15 min, 45 min, 2 h, then a drafting break for anything further), each place a lilac tick at its drive time, the nearest filled; its dimension reads 'all 10 within 2 h 45 min by road'. The Status spend screen gets $0 to the $2.00 limit, an amber tick where the tube turns amber, today's pointer and the dimension '$2.00 left today' (the judges asked for a limit mark so $0.00 still reads). The 404 and 403 scopes get the same weeks scale, empty: 'no contacts on the line'. All of it is inline SVG placed with percentage attributes, and aria-hidden because the page already says it in words.

MAJOR, heads. Each page head is drawn as a callout: the emblem hangs on the head's rule by a leader and stands on the line's enamel as a ring stop. The rule's two ends and the end of its enamel stretch get oblique dimension ticks. Home's section heads and Status's panel heads get balloons: the section's pictogram in a small ring. Her screen gets a ring too, on Status and at the head of Chat on a wide screen.

MAJOR, setup steps. On Home, the loud amber '3' beside 'Finish setting up' (a judges' fault) becomes a chain of numbered balloons joined by leaders (1-2-3), with the step you are at ringed in amber. The folded list of all steps gets the same balloons on a vertical leader. The /setup pages get them too, CSS only: the progress row as balloons on a line with the current one lit, and the step list's numbers as balloons on one leader.

MINOR, emblems. The parent's small page-title tiles and numbered enamel discs become 72px drawn emblems, one per section, in a new 64-unit section of the sprite: 18 of them. The Ideas lamp is drawn on its axis; Plans is a calendar with one day ringed and called out; To do a clipboard calling out the task left to do; Wishes a present with its height measured; Family a grown-up and a child with the child's height marked as on a door frame; Status a graticule with its pulse; Settings a gear drawn as a workshop drawing (pitch circle, bore, keyway); General a house in elevation with its width dimensioned; and one each for AI model, Spending, Messages, Lookups, Connections, Key, History, User and Chat. Pages on a line whose glyph has no drawing of its own (New idea, Edit) wear the line's emblem with the glyph in a small revision balloon. The Settings page's cards wear their section's emblem at 56px, so the emblem system reaches Settings too. Frames and construction lines are one-pixel non-scaling hairlines; the objects are drawn at about 2.25px, so they stay visible at 100% (round 11's 'Drawn' mutant was too thin).

MINOR, kind badges. Each kind's pictogram is redrawn to sit inside a small ring, ring, tint and drawing all in the kind's colour, at 26px in the Ideas table and in Lately added. The sprite has 9 new i-kb-* symbols; the Lucide kind icons stay as they were for the tabs and menus. Every original icon id is kept.
Carried through: the Plans month's weekend columns get the same hatching as the scale, so a free Saturday reads the same way on both drawings. This is a picture over the cells, not a layout change.

Room the pictures needed, nothing else moved: page titles sit about 33px further right for the 4.5rem emblem column; Home's Lately added icon column grows from 1.4rem to 1.75rem; the Settings card icon column grows from 2.75rem to 3.5rem; the Chat head's name and lede sit 0.5rem further from her ring; and each scale adds about 80px under its monitor (Home's left column, the Ideas aside, the Status spend panel, the 404).

One side effect I kept on purpose: the Home section discs numbered 3, 5, 4, 2, which every judge faulted as out of reading order, are now pictogram balloons. The bar's '1 Vera 2 Ideas' numbers are type, not pictures, so they stay the parent's.
The sign-in monitor gets nothing. It shows no data, and anything drawn on it would be the costume the judges already rejected.
title: What's *next* for us? — the parent's words, unchanged, as a dice mutant keeps them. It asks the household ('us') what comes next: weekends, plans and reminders. On this page 'next' speaks with the NEXT UP departure board and now with the scale under it, which draws what is next.

Green share of colour: home 67.3%, ideas 81.6%, chat 89.1%, status 84.0%. Hue entropy: home 0.545, ideas 0.329, chat 0.341, status 0.414. Bright green per mille: home 6.38, ideas 7.83. Small targets under 44px: 0 on Home and on every other page shot, desktop and phone. No sideways scroll anywhere; smallest text 12px, the footer's legal line, as in the parent (the scales' figures are aria-hidden, set at 12.5-14px). Words differ from today by 13.6% on Home, the same as the parent: the title, and every new figure is aria-hidden. No hard check failed. The one WARN is the page's words, carried from the parent. Final full render: ./check.sh palettes/t2-timetable-mut.json, 0 hard checks failed. strengths: One draughtsman's hand on every page. The page-head emblems reach Ideas, Plans, To do, Status, Settings, General, Wishes, Family, Memory and the forms; the Settings cards, Home's heads, the kinds and the setup steps use the same frames, balloons and leaders. It is a system, not a one-off effect.

The monitors' scales carry information the family did not have at a glance. Home's hatched weekends with plan stops show which weekends are free and how the plans are spaced. The Ideas scale shows that most places cluster within half an hour. Status shows the limit and what is left today even at $0.00.

It answers judges' faults using pictures only. The loud amber '3' becomes calm numbered balloons that say 'step 1 of 3'. Home's out-of-order section numbers (3, 5, 4, 2) become pictogram balloons. Spend gets a limit mark.

The emblems read as drawings, not icons in a circle: an axis, one dimension or one callout each, drawn at a weight that holds at 100%. The Family emblem's door-frame height mark and the Settings gear's pitch circle carry some wit.
The light is unchanged. Nothing new glows except the NOW lamp at each scale's datum, so the phosphor list stays short.
No cost to use: 0 small targets, no sideways scroll, no new words for a screen reader, no change in the page's word share.
weaknesses: The scales are small, fine drawings (figures at 12.5-14px on hairlines). At a squint they read as texture under the board, not as a device, and on a phone Home's day labels need a second row when plans are three days apart or less.

The Ideas scale packs eight of ten places into overlapping ticks between 15 and 30 minutes. Everything past two hours sits at one spot after the break, so the drawing cannot show how far beyond. Home's scale clamps anything past four weeks the same way.
'5 plans in 24 days' counts the plans Home lists, which the view caps. With more plans than Home holds, the dimension undercounts.

The drafting marks with no job are decoration: the tick marks on every head rule, and the emblem's leader and stop on the rule. That is the costume risk that sank 'Programme Guide, Drafted'. At 56px on the Settings cards the emblems' centre lines and dimensions all but vanish.
Page titles moved about 33px right to make room for the emblem, and the 72px emblem is the largest non-text mark in the head, so the heads are busier than the parent's.

Coverage is uneven. Chat changes only by the ring round her screen (desktop only). The sign-in monitor is untouched. The spend scale sits below the fold of the Status shot, so the judges' status.png does not show it. To do's timetable gets nothing beyond its head.
Every other fault of the parent is kept by design: '1 Vera 2 Ideas' in the bar reading as counts, wayfinding-yellow links beside amber late, three-line To do rows, copper names.
The forced-colours and more-contrast rules for the SVG drawings are written but untested in a real browser. The warm kind badges (restaurant, seasonal) at a 10% tint may read slightly brown close up.

name: Pocket Traced, Restacked
tagline: Pocket Timeline, Traced with every stop on the line made a row of the page, NEXT's screen across the whole width, denim for every way on that is not the primary, and light words eased half a weight so they do not bloom.
concept: Pocket Timeline, Traced still has one steel line of time down the left, but on Home each stop on that line is now a row of the page, and the tray that belongs to it sits beside it. NOW has the box with setting up beside it. NEXT is a full-width panorama tube: the words on the left, the four weeks traced across the middle of the glass, the radar on the right. Coming up sits beside To do, the other list with dates. Past LATER, the undated things (ideas lately added, the kids' wishes, restaurants) sit beside the dotted run-on. The page reads down the line and then across each row, in Tab order. It feels calmer: denim secondary keys sort out 'what goes or asks' from the one green primary, and every word lit on the dark ground is set half a weight lighter, so it no longer blooms.
companions: Denim (#9db6d6, the parent's link colour) now has a second page-wide job: the secondary role. It colours the ways to start under the box, To do's Search and its four Edit keys, Ideas' Filter, Plans' Earlier and Later, the form's Cancel and the mic. The words are denim, on a slate key with 9%/6% denim mixed in (starter fill samples (39,48,54) against the parent's (28,36,40)), with a 44% denim edge. The rule: green acts, denim goes or asks (links and secondary keys), slate chooses (banks of latched view keys stay slate and light where latched). Everything else is the parent's. The steel line and slate trays stay. Headings stay bone #dcd8cb and labels steel #a9b6bf. Each section's colour appears only on its tile, trail, node and cap. Amber is kept for late and needs-a-look. #6dff9c is on the mark, the one primary, 'next', focus, the live nodes and plates, and the tubes.
decisions: STRUCTURE (rearrange Home). Home was a spine column beside a long shelf of four boxed trays. It is now a stack of rows, one per stop, on one two-column grid (1fr | 24.5rem) so every row splits on the same line: [NOW box | Finish setting up], [NEXT tube, full width], [Coming up | To do], [LATER plate and All plans, full width], [Lately added | kids' wishes + restaurants]. The markup is written in drawn order, so Tab goes box > setup > tube > Coming up > To do > LATER > ideas > wishes (health.json confirms the start of it). On the phone the rows stack in the same order.

The panorama tube. At 70rem and wider, NEXT's glass is three columns: next-up words (19.5rem), the four-week square-pulse trace in the middle (about 500px, starting from the NOW trigger's dashed line), and the radar (8rem). The tube is about 210px tall with no empty lit glass, and the trace reads left to right like the calendar below it. Between 52 and 70rem, and on the phone, it keeps the parent's text+radar over trace layout.

To do plugs in beside Coming up. It is the other list with dates, and it is cut by a lit NOW line. Its tray rises by its top padding, so its head rule runs level with Coming up's rule and the row reads as one line across. LATER is now a real row: its plate and 'All plans' head the undated things. The restaurants link moved out of Lately added into the right column under the wishes. Lately added is 656px wide, so its cartridges fit their names on one line ('Oaks Park roller rink', 'Cannon Beach weekend'). That fixes a wrap the judges faulted, though it was not a separate fix.

The everyday state, not rendered by the harness. Once setting up is done, the template moves To do up beside the box (late tasks are the most 'now' thing there is), puts the wishes and restaurants beside Coming up, and gives Lately added LATER's full row, four across. I checked this by temporarily blanking setup in my template, rendering, and restoring it. The DOM order changes with the state, so Tab still matches what the eye sees.

COLOUR (companion into a new page-wide role). I picked secondary over bar, card-edge, heading and label. Heading or label in denim would read as fake links (a known fault), a bar or edge tint is too faint to register, and ambient is haze. Secondary gives denim one clear meaning ('a way on that is not the primary'), which links already carry. I kept it to words and edges on slate and did not fill keys blue, because indigo starters and keys lost twice (Tuning Dock, Docked Terminal). The sheet did not use --secondary before, so I wired it in: starters, button.secondary, .button.ghost, .clear, mic, .filters button, and To do's Edit summary.

TYPE (light text eased half a weight). IBM Plex Sans and Instrument Sans are variable, so every weight on the dark ground drops exactly half a step through tokens: text 400>350, medium 500>450, semibold 600>550, bold 700>650. That covers heads, the question, date leaves, row titles, keys and the wordmark. Dark words on a lit fill keep their full weight (the primary key, the skip link, OK, ticked boxes). VT323 on the glass is left alone, because its bloom is the point. Plex Mono is static and cannot take half a step. This is the nearest version I could make: figures 14px and up (dates, times, the stop date, the facts column, day names on Plans) ease one whole step to Regular, and the 11-13px legends keep Medium, since small sizes need the weight. The header's written scale is updated to 550 / 450 / 350.

Kept unchanged from the parent: 'What's next for us?' with 'next' lit (a dice mutant keeps its parent's words), the spine, nodes, plates, trace, month tube, To do queue, Chat axis, cartridges, the 'Edit, complete, or snooze' keys, the phone tab bar, the palette tokens (only secondary added) and every glow. Nothing was removed; removed.txt is empty.

strengths: Home's structure now matches the lineage's idea: every stop on the line is a row, and every tray stands level with the stop it belongs to. It is no longer a shelf of four boxes running down the right, which the style judge called the generic part of the page.

The full-width NEXT tube is a panorama: the next plan in words, four weeks traced across the middle of the glass, and the radar, all side by side with no empty lit glass. It is the biggest visible change and it keeps the full phosphor light.

name: Lit Manual, Relit
tagline: The lit manual with its tubes switched back on: real green screens that bloom behind their scanlines, one small lit tube for each drawing's live mark, and a countdown screen on Plans.
concept: Lit Manual with the original tube's light put back wherever the manual shows phosphor, and now on every page. Every monitor is a curved tube in VT323 at three strengths behind bloom and scanlines. Plans gets its own countdown screen, and each drawing's one live mark is a small lit tube: To do's next-due cell, the form field being filled, Chat's newest arrow, Settings' machine and Status's model. The feel is still a calm, well-set manual in bone ink on slate. Its one lit key sits flat on the desk, with the light pooled under it.

name: Ladders, Reset
tagline: Lamps and Ladders with only its type reset: Azeret Mono for the machine and its figures, true small caps on every legend, and every marker hung outside the text edge.
concept: This is Lamps and Ladders with only its typesetting changed, so the panel can see what type alone does to the console. The machine now speaks off the glass in a wide teleprinter mono, the legends read like words engraved on a panel, and every marker (lamp, number, chevron, bullet, prompt) hangs in the margin so the words keep one clean edge. It should feel like the same calm 1969 console, set by a careful compositor.
companions: Unchanged from the parent. Slate (#111716) for every bay under one top rule. Steel (#6f8596 with a #a9c4d8 cap) for "here", today, the waiting dot and the family's side of the log. Pewter rings mean off. Amber (#e3a651) only for "needs a look" and late. Violet (#a191bd) only for the flight plan's solid lines and stop rings. #6dff9c stays on the short list: the mark and cursor, Send, the lit key word "next", focus, the jewel lamps, the ladders' heads, the live leg and the tubes. The small-caps legends take the parent's `label` grey, and the new mono takes the colours of the figures it replaced.
decisions: THE NEW MONO: Azeret Mono replaces IBM Plex Mono everywhere `--code` reached. That covers the rail's figures, hop dates and times, log stamps, the day rule, task ids, due times, table figures, ring and step numbers, the track and radar scale words, date inputs, `code` and `pre`, the bar's wordmark and the foot. I chose it over the other five by setting each in a mock of the rail, the hops and the log. Red Hat Mono's zero reads as the letter O, which fails padded readouts. Fira Code and Victor Mono read as code editors, and Geist Mono is too close to Plex Mono to be seen. Spline Sans Mono was the close second: I rendered Home in both. Azeret's wide, round, monoline forms read as a teleprinter or character generator, so the machine's voice is plainly apart from Plex, the family's words.

TUNING THE MONO: Azeret's figures are as tall as Plex Mono's (cap 0.70em) but about 8% wider and darker (x-height 0.55em against 0.52em). So rail figures go to weight 450 with -0.015em tracking. Inside Plex text ($0.00, '4 open', '3 of 4') it is set at 14px/500, stamps and ids at 12px, hop dates and times at 13px/450, and inline code at 0.84em. I found that Azeret's tabular-figure glyphs drop its slashed zero, so wherever the parent asked for 'tabular-nums slashed-zero' I ask for the slash alone (every mono figure is tabular anyway). The parent's padded '05' now reads as a figure, not 'O5'.

TRUE SMALL CAPS: I tested every library face in Chromium. Plex Sans, Plex Sans Condensed and all six rolled monos have no smcp, and the body's `font-synthesis: none` would render plain lowercase. The only sans with real smcp and c2sc is Barlow Condensed (Source Serif 4 and Literata are serifs). So legends get a fourth family, Barlow Condensed, for this one job. Engraved-plate small caps suit a flight console. All-small-caps with 0.05em tracking (0.08em on the log's call signs, which replace the parent's 0.14em tracked uppercase) goes on the rail labels, field labels and legends, column and month heads, dl terms, eyebrows, kinds, state words, tags, the lamp key, date chips, the 'From' label and the case's 'Spent today'. Its small caps stand 0.58em tall, so legends are set at 15px (8.7px glyphs, about the old 13px label's capitals). Checkbox and 'Send where I am' labels and Home's question stay in sentence case. The tubes keep VT323 capitals, because a 1969 character generator had no small caps.

HANGING: I set one rule: a marker that leads a line sits in the margin, so the words keep one edge. The amber bar before Late or Needs a look hangs in its rail window, so the legend stands on the figure's edge. Setup's step numbers are pulled out between the ladder gutter and the head, so the steps read from 'Finish setting up''s edge, and the rules still run from the gutter. Next up's '>' prompt hangs in the glass margin, so '4 more on the radar' stands under 'Silver Falls hike'. Disclosure chevrons hang ('Add something to do', 'Everything else', 'Exact position and travel times'), and so do the lamp key's first lamp and the lamp before Vera's 'Ready'. So do `.tips` bullets, and the General page's numbered steps move into the tile gutter. The log's '└─' becomes a hung '└'.

BENT AND LEFT OUT: I bent three hangs to the nearest version that does not hurt. On the phone's 12-16px margins the markers come back inside, because a hang there would cross a divider or the edge of the screen. The Settings cards' state lamp, the Ideas capture's chevron (inside a 16px well) and icons such as the plug before 'Google Calendar is not connected' are not hung: icons belong to their words, and those margins cannot hold a marker. Quotes have almost nothing to hang on. Every quotation mark on the rendered pages is mid-line (“tonight”, “end_turn”), and CSS cannot see a quote that opens a chat line, so the quote half of the roll only sets `q` in typographer's marks.

NOTHING ELSE MOVED: colours, tokens, glow numbers, layout, templates and words are all the parent's. The mutant has no markup of its own, and every change is in `variants/t2-console-mut/sheet.css`: the `--code` and `--legend` faces in `:root`, then one marked block at the end. I removed a trial widening of the hop time column because Azeret fits in the parent's grid. I also rewrote the sheet's header note to describe the new type system.
title: "Tell Vera what’s *next*." This is the parent's title, kept word for word because a dice mutant keeps its parent's words; only its type sits beside new legends. It says the job as an invitation to tell Vera the next thing to plan, and 'next' ties to Next up and the countdown ladders. The judges found it narrower than the whole job, since ideas kept for someday and wish lists are not 'next'.
measures: The full render passes with 0 hard checks failed. ink_on_bg is 13.17 and brand_on_bg 15.28, the parent's, since no colour changed. Green share of colour: Home 37.3%, Ideas 63.1%, Chat 44.9%, Status 20.3%. Hue entropy: Home 0.635, Ideas 0.498, Chat 0.59, Status 0.611. Small targets on Home: 0 of 63 under 44px (none under 24px). There is no sideways scroll on any page. Smallest text is 11.76px, inline `code` on General (at 0.8125em it measured 11.38px, so I raised it). One guideline is missed, as it was for the parent: Home's words differ 20.2% from today (the parent's title and rail; this mutant changed no words).
strengths: The figures now have a voice of their own. Azeret's wide teleprinter forms make the readout rail, the hop dates and times, the log stamps and the task ids read as the machine talking, clearly apart from Plex's family words. That is visible on every page, not in a corner.

The legends are true small caps, not faux ones: Barlow Condensed's real smcp and c2sc glyphs at an even weight. The rail, the field labels, the month heads, the kinds, the lamp key and the log's call signs now read as one engraved-plate system. The call signs lose the 0.14em tracked capitals that type judges disliked.

Hanging gives the page cleaner edges wherever there was room. 'Late' and 'Needs a look' stand on their figure's edge, setup's steps read from the head's edge, '4 more on the radar' lines up under the title on the glass, folded heads match open ones, and the lamp key's 'On' lines up with the text under it.
The parent's slashed zero now actually shows, fixed at the level of the face (Azeret's tnum glyphs drop it). Padded readouts read as figures ('Ø5'), not as 'O5'.

It is a coherent written type system with one job per face (read / heads / machine / legends / glass) and a scale noted in the sheet: 44 / 36 / 22 / 16 / 15 legend / 14 / 12. Nothing else moved, so the panel can judge the typesetting alone.
weaknesses: It breaks the IBM Plex superfamily the type judges praised and adds a face. There are now four families (Plex, Azeret, Barlow Condensed, VT323), and Barlow is there only because no Plex face and none of the six rolled monos cuts small caps. Barlow's highway-sign lineage is the same face whose condensed 'trail-sign' heads faded in round 6, though here it is only 15px legends.

Small caps are smaller than their font size suggests: at 15px the glyphs are about 8.7px tall. Long field labels in small caps ('BOOK THIS FAR AHEAD (DAYS)', 'HOME TOWN OR AREA') read slower than the parent's sentence case, and figures inside small-caps tags ('10 LOOKED UP') stay full-height lining figures.
The quote half of the roll does almost nothing visible. Every quotation mark on the rendered pages is mid-line, so none hangs; only `q` gets typographer's marks.

The hang rule has exceptions a reader can spot. Markers come back inside on the phone. The Settings cards' 'Needs a look' lamp, the Ideas capture chevron and leading icons are not hung. The 'Ready' and lamp-key lamps hang into the page margin outside the bays' edge and may read as stray dots. The rail's hung amber bar sits only about 5px from its window divider.

Azeret is about 8% wider and darker than Plex Mono. Even a size down, its figures in running text ('$0.00 of the $2.00' on Status) stand out more than the parent's did. The slashed zero also makes the parent's zero-padding ('05', '01', '09'), which every judge asked to drop, more conspicuous.
All the parent's non-type faults stay by design: the zero-padded rail, the unlabelled T-minus ladders, the slate gap in the Status head, the title 'next', and the rail before the box in Tab order.

name: Switchboard, Metered
tagline: The switchboard with its instruments drawn: today's spend on a lit moving-coil meter, each cell of lights headed by a ring of its lamps, what it has cost in printed bars, each place's own legend on its key (lit from behind on the one you are on), and the mark as the page's monitor in miniature.
concept: Switchboard, Trued with only its pictures changed, as the dice rolled them. The machine's measures are now drawn the way a panel draws them. What is live now glows in the phosphor: a moving-coil spend meter on the glass, and rings of lamps round each cell's picture. What is past is printed matte on the plate: bars in bone, sage, steel and pewter. The six places get their own square-cut legends, outlined at rest and filled as if lit from behind on the page you are on. The mark becomes the page's own graphite monitor in miniature, with a smile on lit glass and a power light in its chin. It should feel like the same calm bone-and-slate panel, now with real instruments on it that give off light only where something is live.
companions: These are the parent's companions, each given a job inside the new pictures. Bone (#cdc6b5) draws the printed cost bars ("By kind of call", "Sent") and the faces in the lamp rings. Sage lit (#92dfa7) marks tokens read from the cache, the cheap share. Steel (#93b4c8) marks tokens written to the cache and stays the colour of the current key. Pewter (#8794a2) draws the ring's thin arcs for lights that are off, the scale ticks under the bars and the "Back" tokens. Amber (#eaa76b) keeps its one meaning: the meter's last quarter before the limit and its limit tick, and a "needs a look" segment in a ring. The graphite bezel (#272b2b) is the mark's case. Everything else is the parent's, unchanged.
decisions: MAJOR, the instrument panel on Status. (1) The spend tube's ASCII bar '[....] 0%' becomes an SVG moving-coil meter on the glass (_ui.html spend_meter). It is a 100° arc scale from $0 to the day's limit, square-root spaced as a VU meter's is, so a few cents still move the needle. Its ticks are labelled 0, .20, .50, 1 and 2 from the limit. The last quarter is an amber band, and the limit is a long amber tick. The needle has a hot core in a halo with a drop-shadow bloom and runs down under a black pivot dome. A dashed ghost needle with a drag pointer marks the average day of the last 30 (dollars/days, $0.04). name: Relaid, Finished
tagline: Signal Box Relaid finished in its own grammar: the family's week as steel track on slate, every count standing at its line's buffer, and #6dff9c lit only on the job, the box and what is live.
concept: Signal Box Relaid, finished in its own grammar and not merged into Branch Lines. The family's week is steel track on green-black slate: straight runs, one 45-degree chamfer at each turn, a terminus ring where a line begins and a T buffer where it ends, with #6dff9c lit only where attention belongs. Every count stands at its line's buffer. The one lamp legend is Status's tally and now draws five signals in five shapes. The form is a line whose lit stop sits on the focused field's own centre line, and the plans carry one cool period colour. It should feel like a calm, exact signal box at night: the question, the box and the live lamps are lit, and everything else is matte steel and slate.
companions: Steel #a7c4d8 is the one main companion, and it has a job. It marks "here": the latched cell with its steel run, and today's cell on the month under a 3px steel cap. It also draws the hollow to-come and waiting rings, the links and the ends of lines. Its darker kin draw the diagram: rail #607385, wire #4f5e6b, buffer #8a9aa8, pewter #6f7b85, and #2b333a, the unlit lens that now means off. The plans' cyan #70dcf4 is a measured period colour. It is a 2px cap at 70% on every plan plate (Home's fortnight and the Plans list) and the to-come ring on a plan, so Home is not grey and green alone. Sage #86d9a6 means done. It is also the lit edge of a row's afterglow and the halo a row's stop takes when it is pointed at. Amber means late or needs a look and nothing else: '2 late', the late stamps and lamps, the setup board's edge, and now the page still on the installer's password. The kinds keep their colour in the ring alone (terracotta, moss, wheat, lilac, cyan, pink), and a ring brightens to its full kind colour when its row is pointed at. Bone #ebe6da carries the heads and figures.

Five signals in five shapes, one legend for every page. Live is the lit phosphor lamp. Waiting (and to come) is the hollow steel ring. Off is an unlit lens: a #2b333a disc in a 1.5px pewter rim. Not set up is a hollow pewter ring crossed by the lineage's own 45-degree bar (the chamfer, in pewter); it replaces the dashed ring, which read as a spinner at 12px. Needs a look is filled amber. A second rule holds on every page: the machine's words and marks are phosphor, the board and its rails are slate and steel, and what the family wrote or put on the calendar is ink.

Amber is only for late and the setup edge. Sage #86d9a6 is the word 'now', a done tick and the row afterglow. The kind rings are grounded: terracotta #df987c for restaurants, moss #b5c87d for outings and wheat #c3a85d for seasonal ideas. #6dff9c is lit only where something is live: the mark, 'planning', Send, the box, focus, the now lamps and their runs, working lamps and the tubes.

name: Departures, Posted

concept: This is Night Departures with the faults the judges named taken out, and the station's own way of printing things carried to every page. Vera's line runs down Home's middle, from her screen through the lit "What's our plan?" box and the ways to start to a lit terminus, with the departure board standing to the right of the question it answers. Every list, on every page, is posted the same way: what it is, a dotted leader, then the fact in condensed tabular figures. It should feel like a quiet station after dark: matte slate, warm ink and pewter rails, one steel-denim link colour and small enamel roundels naming each line. The original tube's light shows only where something is live.

The one row that needs a look reads 'Needs a look  Still the password the …', which hides the very reason. Connections, Messages and Personality are cut too. A station directory is one column. Drop the 64rem two-column rule and set the directory to one column at every width, capped at about 62rem, with .section-state allowed its full line. Put the lede on one line at --t-body with max-width:none, beside or just under 'Vera' (it fits in the 56rem meridian), and trim .page-chat main's top padding, so the box and Send are on the first screen. Also, every Vera bubble has a 24% phosphor edge, so the 'only the newest stop lit' rule is diluted, and Chat measures 97.6% green. Give .said-bot .bubble the steel --card-edge at rest and light only .stop#latest's bubble edge (about a 35% brand mix). The newest stop then reads alone, and bone and steel-denim carry more of the page.

PLANS MONTH (.month td.outside, td.past; plans_month.html lede). Sinking every day outside the month to #0a0d0c puts tomorrow's Silver Falls hike and Sunday's roller rink in the darkest cells, while the gone-by September weeks sit on the lit slate. Push past numerals further down, for example color-mix(in srgb,var(--faint) 70%,var(--bg)), so faint reads as gone rather than as one grey step. TO DO ROW (.tasks-tt > li.task grid and areas; .late button.tick::before; .late .stop). The leader runs from the title to the owner. The fact that matters, the due words, then sits alone across a gap of about 150px ('Alex ........ [gap] was due 3 days ago'), which breaks the departure grammar the rest of the page teaches. Reorder the areas to 'stamp stop tick title who leader due edit': the person icon and name in ink-2 right after the title, and the leader carrying the eye to 'was due 3 days ago' or 'due tomorrow'. A row with no due date gets no leader. A late row also stacks four amber marks: the stamp, a filled stop, a ringed and haloed tick well, and the words. Keep the tick well neutral, and draw the late stop as a 2px amber ring on --bg, as the sheet's own rule says ('never a fill'). The stamp, the ring and the words are enough.

KINDS VERSUS LINES (.kind-activity, .kind-trip/.kind-day_trip, .kind-show, .kind-event/.kind-other). The key's second mark, and the line on pages that hold no time. That makes Status's line a state column, and the '1 needs a look' figure shows up there when it is true. Then rename k-on in the key to 'A section'. On Settings, all nine `.section-card` icon tiles glow in --lit green. Set those glyphs in --label steel, so the only colours on that page are the lit current page in the bar and the amber card that needs a look.

Two small fixes to the system and the phone. First, the sheet's header comment and the `.day` comment still say the figure is 'large in Plex Mono', but it is drawn in Plex Sans 400 tabular. Correct them, and write the type steps down as drawn, because the winner's sheet becomes the standard. Second, on the phone the Settings key's chevron floats in the key's top-right corner, apart from its word. Under 40rem, hide the chevron on `.menu > summary`, or set it inline after 'Settings' at 11px so the four 48px keys read alike. Also remove the space before the comma in Home's hidden row text ('Oaks Park roller rink , Sunday 4 October'), which comes from whitespace after plan_where(entry) before `<span class="sr">`.

firstDraft.name: Pocket Diary
firstDraft.concept: Pocket Timeline's steel line of time, set the way a pocket diary sets its pages. Every date on every page is printed as a diary prints a day: a large figure, with the month over the weekday beside it. The figures down Home's rows are the same figures as the pulses on the NEXT trace above, and pointing at a row lights its pulse. The weekend, the unit the family plans in, is shaded in light on the glass, washed in steel on the slate and set in bone in the type. The key to the line's five square marks sits inside the cover, in every footer, where each page's dotted run-on ends. The feel is a calm slate handheld you keep in a pocket. Phosphor light sits only where something is now: the NOW and NEXT plates, today's lit figure, the next pulse, the weekend bands on the glass, live lamps and the key's first square.

name: Lit Manual, Railed
tagline: The family's operator manual, lit: every figure touches its rows, and one lit NOW line runs across every list in time.
concept: Lit Manual's plates, with one rule made to hold on every page: a figure touches its rows. Any list in time is drawn as a rail in the figure column. Each row's day and stop sit level with that row, and a dotted leader runs over the hairline into it. NOW is a lit phosphor line that leaves the rail and crosses the list; on the plan rails the line stays lit down to the next plan's stop. The chat's thread is its own sequence diagram, with each arrow's leader running to whoever spoke, and Status leads with its wiring. The feel is a calm technical manual on slate and bone, lit by one green tube per page, with light only on what is live.
companions: Blueprint is the one cool companion, used only in drawings: #6f88b3 lines and #9fb4d6 words on the slate drawing sheet (#0f161c, 12/48 grid). The sheet sits under every rail (To do, Home's Coming up, the Plans list and Recently, the month's week rail), the chat's lifelines and their leaders, the Status wiring, the tally, the machine and the form's anatomy. #9fb4d6 also underlines prose links, and a 55% blueprint line underlines head links. "Here" is steel, never a slab: a 24% steel tint (about #1c2328) under a 2px #a9c4d8 cap, with the label in bone. It is used in the bar, the phone tab bar, tabs, Every kind, the settings parts (where the ring and numeral also turn steel), the select's chosen row and today on the month. Amber #f1af64 means late or needs a look, and appears only as words, 3px row edges, rings and filled late stops. Bone ink (#dcd8ca, heads #e8e2d0) sits on green-black #0b100d. Each kind's colour lives only in its .75rem square. #6dff9c is exact and goes on the mark, the one primary, 'plan', focus, lamps, the NOW lines (and the stretch of rail from NOW to the next plan), the next plan's stop, the newest arrow, the lit port, the tally's next due and the three green screens.
decisions: THE RAIL as shared parts in _ui.html (rail_mark, rail_day, now_rule) and the sheet (.railed, .rail-mark, .rail-date, .rail-dot, .now-rule). A railed list is one subgrid over the figure column and the words, so every mark is a cell of its own row. The edition's rule is written in _ui.html's header: A FIGURE TOUCHES ITS ROWS.

Home's Coming up rail now runs over every plan, the next one included. Stop 1 is Thu 1 Oct, 'Silver Falls hike ··· 10:00 tomorrow', straight under NOW. It is the rail's one live mark: rail_mark(state='next') draws a #e4fff0 core in the two-layer halo, and the halo breathes while the core and its numeral stay put. The stretch of rail from the NOW lamp down to that stop is lit too, so the figure reads 'now, then next' as one trace. The other plans are numbered 2-5. The count is said once: 'Coming up · Next up, then 4 more · All plans', which agrees with the tube's '4 more on the radar'. Caption: 'Fig. 1 Coming up by day: the lit stop is next, the lit line is now.'

The Plans list uses the same grammar: NOW is lit at the top, the next stop and the line down to it are lit, and the caption is 'Each plan on its day, numbered in order: the lit stop is next, the lit line is now.' The facts stop at 46rem, so no leader runs to the far edge. Recently keeps a quiet rail of hollow, dim stops with no NOW.

Home's greeting: square, with the words first at the left and the portrait Next up tube at the right (radar 9.5rem, VT323 at three strengths). The pool rises from under the tube, with scanlines at 3.5% masked there and a blueprint whisper at the top left. The ways to start are 44px keys, 8px apart.

Home's To do sits beside the rail: neutral ticks, a 3px amber edge and amber 'was due' words on late rows, and its own lit NOW between the late tasks and the rest. The head reads 'To do · 2 late · All 4'. '2 late' is an amber link to /tasks#late, which lands on the first late row with the kit's E10 flash. The phone's jump row stays: '4 more plans · 4 to do · 2 late'.

Plans month: THE WEEK RAIL is the table's first column, on the drawing sheet, and its right edge is the plate hairline. Each week's stop sits on the week's top edge. Its range, count and weekend squares sit inside the week's own row: the range is level with the day numerals at .5rem, and under it are '3 plans' and two 12px squares, 4px apart. A week gone that held nothing folds to 2.75rem, and past weeks drop their weekend squares, so this week, its NOW run and the Fig. 1 caption rise onto the first screen. In this week the stop is the lit lamp, 'NOW' sits beside it inside this week's row, and the lit line runs along the week's top edge over the hairline to today's latched cell and its lamp.

Chat: the thread is the diagram. A 60px lanes row heads the figure column: her 2rem screen (bloom, scanlines, one glyph fall), then the family's initials in 2rem steel squares at 96 and 164px, with no names, since the squares repeat the ones beside their lines. Dotted lifelines run down each line's cell, and each arrow (numbered 1-4) sits level with its speaker line at 24px. A 1px dotted blueprint leader runs on from each arrow over the hairline to whoever spoke. For her lines it ends at her glyph at the words' edge; for the family's it continues as a flex:1 dotted rule through their own line up to '19:47 Sam'. Pointing at a line lights its arrow and turns its leader sage. The newest arrow is the live mark, with an E10 arrival flash. The composer's box, From row and Send are all on the first screen.

To do: the rail with NOW in the kit's two-layer light, late rows with a neutral tick, a 3px amber edge and 'Late · was due 3 days ago', '#4' faint after the title, 'Edit' with its pencil at the right, and 'No active reminder' in faint. Fig. 1, the tally, now draws true squares (28 units, stacked 6 apart) in each owner's column. The next due is a 2px lit outline round its own square. The legend's 'Next due' key is a matte steel outline, so the lit outline is the figure's one light.

Status: the head spans, and its three readings are links at the right of the title's row. 'What is working' is led by the wiring (sticky), with a one-line 'What a lamp says' under it. Pointing at a key or connection row lights its own port and wire. 'What it has cost' is led by the page's one green screen, the original's spend readout ($0.00 in VT323 2.5rem, 'of $2.00 today', '[..........] 0%', 'about $0.04 a day', power light), re-lit amber from 75% of the limit and red past it, and aria-hidden. Table column heads are now sentence-case labels in Plex Sans, not lowercase mono.

Settings: the overview's figure column ends in 'Needs a look': an amber ring 8 and 'Sign-in and security: still the installer’s password' as a 44px link. In the list, the Sign-in row says 'Needs a look' in plain amber words with no frame. On section pages the machine is capped at 13rem, the list is labelled 'Parts', and the current part shows 'here' by the latch alone (a steel ring and numeral, bone label). The drawing keeps the page's one lit part.

Ideas: the radar tube leads the head. 'Show one kind' is a visible label over the kinds control, whose rows are 44px links; on the phone they re-lay as a wrapping row of 44px keys above the list. The list reads #id | kind | title | drive (right-aligned tabular mono under 'Drive, about') | way | For.

Light (kit): --lit-mark is two layers (2px .85, 10px .38). The NOW lines are 3px .8 and 14px .32 with a #e4fff0 lamp core. Rows light their own stop, arrow or port in 0.12s and let go over 1.2s. There is one green screen per page. E3 is on the one primary, E4 on fields and E6 is the top haze. E10 works on anchors, and E20 keeps the lamps breathing. Reduced motion, more contrast and forced colours cover the new parts: the lit next stop, the leaders and the lit trace.

Type on a 24px line: title 48/48 condensed; Home's question 52 (clamped), the largest head; head 28/32; lede 18/28 (16/24 on the phone) set pretty; body 16/24; small 15/24; --t-label 13/20 semibold, sentence case, untracked, for every legend. Mono is only for dates, times and figures in columns, always tabular. The kids' '0 open' is now sans with no slashed zero. Apostrophes are curly in the templates and in displayed data lines (titles, Status details, Settings states).

Footer: the mark alone in the figure column. The tagline sits in the words column on the mark's baseline, with the legal line under it on one line in --t-small, faint, so the version no longer splits from its number.
title: "Tell Vera what to *plan*." ('plan' is lit, E1.) It is the manual's own voice, an instruction that says who hears you and what the box is for: the family plans by telling Vera. 'Plan' is the job, and it covers weekends, ideas worth keeping, the calendar and reminders. The line fits one line on a phone at 32px, and it stays the textarea's <label>. It was the lineage's best title (first for style, interaction and skeptic in tour round 1), the brief kept it, and the critic asked to keep it. No other glow on the greeting claims 'plan'.

name: Gauged Manual
tagline: The family's operator manual, gauged: every plate led by a figure drawn from its own data, with a round tube where a live number needs one and pencil, break lines and dimensions for the rest.
concept: Lit Manual's grammar is unchanged: a plate, a figure on a slate drawing sheet drawn from the page's own data, and one lit mark in each. Its thin places now carry four drafting devices, each replacing what was there. Plans and Status each get a round green tube on a blueprint instrument ring, the month folds its empty weeks behind a break mark, the kinds are a pencil-hatched legend, and "in 4 days" is drawn as a dimension from a common NOW datum. It should feel like a calm, well-set technical manual with two small instruments switched on: the tube's light is back where a live number is, and the rest is matte pencil, blueprint and bone.
companions: Blueprint (#6f88b3 line, #9fb4d6 lettering) is the drawing ink. It draws the sheets, the rails, the instrument rings and their ticks, the dimension lines, the break marks, the chat's margin arrows and every drawing's lettering (now one rule: 13px Plex Mono in sentence case). It is also the 1px line under head links, whose words are bone. The seven kinds are pencils: each kind's colour laid 78% over graphite #8f948c (outing is moss #a3c690, never phosphor). They appear only as -45° hatching inside a pencil border: the 18–20px legend squares, the Kind filter's bars, and now the kind square in the idea page's anatomy drawing. They stay at least 14.8 apart for typical sight. Steel #a9c4d8 marks "here" as a tint plus a 2px latch (bar, tabs, today's cell, "Every kind"). Amber means only late or needs a look: words, a 3px row edge, a ring, and the spend tube re-lit from 75% of the limit. Bone ink #dcd8ca is used for the words. Full #6dff9c is kept to the mark, Send and the page's one primary, the lit "plan", focus, lamps, the NOW lines, the newest chat mark, the tubes (Next up, the radar and the two round gauges) and today's dimension.
decisions: G1 round tubes on Plans (list and month) and on Status only. Each is a 12.5rem crt sunk in the slate sheet inside a 1.25px blueprint ring 8px outside the glass, with E13 blur, E14 scanlines and falloff, and E16 power-on from opacity .05. The E12 spill is now 0 0 90px -18px at 55% and the sheet no longer clips it, so the grid round the ring picks up the green. The round glass is lit from its middle and falls off at the rim. firstDraft.name: Lamps and Legs
firstDraft.concept: This merges the lineage's two tied designs. It keeps every lit instrument from Lamps and Ladders: the jewels, the live leg, the moving-coil meter and the tubes, now behind Aglow's curved glass. Where Lamps and Ladders used codes, it uses Go's plain words and numbers: each leg's length over its arc, stops numbered to the rows, 'Working'/'Off' written in the annunciator windows, due dates on two lines, and each count said once. The page should feel like a calm slate console at night: the eye goes to the few things that are lit, and nothing on it needs a legend to learn.

name: Master Caution
tagline: The flight console with one amber light: a master caution band says what waits on an admin, the flight plan is drawn into the weeks still to fly, and every tube switches on with a roll of light.
concept:
This is Lamps and Ladders kept as a night-shift instrument panel: jewelled pilot lamps, the moving-coil meter, the radar tube and the violet flight plan. Its weakest parts are swapped for three grafts rebuilt in the console's own terms.
- A master caution band, the same component on Home, Status and Settings. It says in one 64px line what waits on an admin, with its amber lamp lit from behind in a sunk window.
- A Plans month whose flown weeks fold away (a run of empty ones becomes one strip that says so). A line of flight-plan legs is drawn over each week still to fly, in the same columns as the week under it.
- A bar of light that rolls once down every tube as it switches on, a tenth of a second after the page loads.

It should feel calm and exact, with light only on what is live: the day's clock, the next hop, the box being written in, the lit bus between the models that answer, and the one amber light.

firstDraft.name: Master Caution
firstDraft.concept: This is Lamps and Ladders kept as an instrument panel: jewelled pilot lamps, the moving-coil meter, the radar tube and the violet flight plan. Its weakest parts are swapped for three grafts rebuilt in the console's own terms. First, the master caution: one 64px amber-edged band, the same on Home, Status and Settings, lit only while something waits on an admin. name: Switchboard, Settled
tagline: The videotex sommaire settled into two tiers: the terminal and its one hot word first, Plans, To do and Ideas as the lit list cells, the rest of the service as one contents cell, and every inner page opening on a short green screen at the head of its register.
concept: Home is the service's contents page in two tiers. The first tier is Vera's graphite terminal, with 'What’s the plan?' typed on its glass and only 'plan' running hot, then setting-up and the three lists the family keeps (Plans with Next up and its radar on its own tube, To do, Ideas), each headed by one contents line under a cool 2px cap with its icon in its colour. The second tier is the rest of the service as one contents cell, with its lamp key as its last line. Every inner page opens on a matte plate beside a register headed by a short, wide green tube that says what the rows don't. The feel is a calm bone-and-slate panel where only the machine gives off light: the tubes, one hot word, Send, the lamps, focus and the lit edge of the row you point at.
companions: Bone #cdc6b5 is the page's own ink. It carries accents, the contents lines of every page that isn't a list, Wishes, the initial tiles, the arrows on the ways to start, the words on the month's plan chips and the service's numerals. The three lists share a cool period set, used only as 2px caps, head icons, numerals, tinted leaders and a few words in the content: sky #9ccdf8 for Plans ('in 4 days', and the weekday and month of every plan date at 70% into dim), teal #83d5d4 for To do (the open tick boxes are edged at 45% into the grey), and steel periwinkle #a7ace4 for Ideas. Amber #eaa76b means setup, needs a look or late, and nothing else. Steel #a9c4d8 means 'here': the bar key, the latched filter key and today's ring on the month. The kinds no longer borrow section colours. They are an earth set with its own hues: clay #ae9a8f for restaurants, straw #c6af75 for activities, olive #8d9a5c for outings, denim #7290a8 for trips and day trips, mauve #c09fb7 for shows, rust #b87e75 for seasonal (the `seasons` token, pulled down to C .074), and periwinkle for events and other. Everything else is graphite and slate. The bright #6dff9c appears only on the mark and caret, the glass, the hot word, the prompt, Send and the one primary per page, focus, the lit lamps and LEDs, the radars and the head tubes.
decisions: Home keeps the brief's two tiers, but the grid now spans five rows so each column's cells follow on without a hole. While setting up, the left column runs terminal, To do, then the service, and the right runs setup, Plans, then Ideas. The brief's 'ideas service' row left 142px of dead slate, because the right column (setup, Plans, service) is 142px taller than the left. Swapping which column holds Ideas and which holds the service ends both columns at 1247px. Plans is stretched by the 33px left over, and its source note moves to the foot under a hairline, so the extra space reads as a pause, not a hole. Once setup is done, Ideas goes back under To do and the service under Plans ('term plans / todo plans / todo service / ideas service'). The source order is unchanged, so the phone's order and the Tab order are the same as before. Home is 1433px, down from 1481.
The lamp key is the service cell's last line, under a 35% bone hairline. The map-foot and its 'key key' grid row are gone.

`contents_line` takes a `glyph`. Plans, To do and Ideas carry their icon at 1.35rem in their colour, as the inner plates do. Their 2px leaders are drawn 42% into the section colour, so each list's head line is its own.

The service's sub-lines now hang at one indent and one pitch. The fix is `.service .svc-sub`, which outranks `ul.plain`, on desktop and on the phone. A note that only extends the count ('2 off') is regular and dim, while a warning note keeps its amber numeral.

The terminal's question is at --t-tube-q 3.3rem, so the lit 'plan' is the largest thing on Home. The well is `min-height:3em` on both desk and phone and grows with field-sizing. On the phone the ways to start are set 1+2 as on the desk, and the locate row is tightened, so the case is about 470px tall instead of 565px.

The case sits one layer above the cell under it (z-index), so its E7 pool falls as a faint breath on To do's lip, the way a lit screen lights the desk. The case no longer has slate under it to take the pool. To keep the page calm, the pool is at 26% brand and the glass-lit deck lip at 9%.

To do: the # column numbers the rows in display order (1-4), not by ids. Edit is a ghost key (the bone pencil and its word) that shows its key face only on the row pointed at or in use. The head tube's bars are one column in time order (Late, This week, Later, No date) at the tube's line pitch. Each bar is still a 44px key: the hit areas overlap by a third, and the hover fill is clipped to the line.

Every head screen spans its register. On the month, Earlier and Later are a second 44px bank ('Month') in the module. The tube adds 'Next: Silver Falls hike / Thu 1 Oct, 10:00 [TOMORROW]' beside the weekend line. Past weeks with nothing on fold to a 2.4rem line of dates, so the week to come gets the room. The plate says what it counts: '2 to come by 4 Oct'.

Status: 'The lights' key sits in the module under 'Change the limit'. The spend tube spans the register, and its meter is forty cells, so it runs the width of the glass. 'SPENT TODAY, ABOUT' is an inverse caps legend like the other tubes' legends. The cost tables are set `auto-fill minmax(22rem,1fr)` with the first column nowrap, so 'answering the family' holds one line. Model names use non-breaking hyphens in 'Last call' and in 'Calls that ended oddly'.

There is one field system. The new-idea form and every settings group share `--label-col: 12rem` and `--field-max: 30rem`: a label column, the box at its measure, and help at 15px dim under the box. Every form control sits in column 2 and the mic in column 3, so all boxes end on one edge (1073px). The settings' three-up boxes became one row per setting, so 'Default (Vancouver · UTC-07:00)' holds one line. There is a phone layout for both.

Labels: `.cell-label` is set at the label step ('After Next up', 'Lately added' are 13px/600 dim). The plate note's numeral is set at the count size ('4 open · 2 late' on the To do plate), and a note that is not a warning is dim and regular ('6 calls'). Tags and settings' 'changed' mark are Plex Sans 600 at the label step, untracked and not uppercased, so capitals are the glass's alone.

Typesetting: register leaders are a 1px dotted hairline (line-2 at 75%). Contents lines, Settings' lines included, keep the 2px leader. There is one duration format, '2 h 45 min', on the Ideas tube and in the register. Single-digit minutes take a figure space ('2 h  5 min' stands under '2 h 10 min'). Plan dates tint the weekday and month in sky on Home and on the Plans list.
Page numbers: the last stray ones (601 and 602 on the Wishes lines) are removed, so numbers live only on Home's map.
title: What’s the *plan*? It is the lineage's title and the tour's favoured one, kept from one source (ask_title() in _ui.html, used by Home and _ask.html). On the glass, 'What’s the' is set at the tube's dim strength with one tight halo, and 'plan' alone has the white-hot core and E1's two-layer halo. It is now 3.3rem, the largest head on Home. measures: Final full render: 0 hard checks failed, 1 guideline warned. The service cell now reads as one true contents list: one hanging indent, one pitch, quiet notes, the amber needs-a-look numeral, and the lamp key as its last line.

Tubes that say what the rows don't. To do's time-ordered bars are 44px keys with Late in amber, beside NEXT DUE. Ideas shows its places radar with Nearest and Furthest. The month gives its weekend and the next plan, with gone weeks folded. Status has a forty-cell spend meter across the glass.

Typesetting throughout. Sentence case and untracked labels everywhere, with capitals only in inverse legends on the glass. Two leader weights, so heads outrank rows. Tabular figures with single-digit minutes set on a figure space. One duration format. Non-breaking hyphens in model names. One count pattern: a condensed numeral, then its word.
0 small targets on every page. The bar LED marks 'here'. Page numbers survive only as the map's index.

Ideas (72%), Chat (81%) and Status (75%) are greener still.

The Home arrangement depends on state. While setting up, the service sits under To do, beside Ideas. Once setup is done, Ideas moves back under To do and the service under Plans, with about 110px of slack at the foot of the right column. I could not render that set-up state to check it. The bottom row now reads service then Ideas left to right, while the Tab order goes Ideas then service, so there is a small zig-zag.
Plans is stretched by 33px while setting up. The foot note sits under a hairline at the cell's foot, but a sharp eye will see the pause.

On a phone the To do and Ideas registers still come after their head tube. On To do the first rows start below the first screen. I kept DOM order equal to visual order rather than reorder with CSS, which would break the Tab order.

Kinds still pair up: Trip and Day trip share denim, and Event and Other share periwinkle, told apart only by icon and word. Event's periwinkle is also the Ideas section colour.
The page's words differ from today's by up to 35% (Plans, Ideas, Home), because the sommaire, the month's tube and its keys name things in their own words.

LABELS and COUNTS: two brief items missed. (a) `.cell-label` has only a margin rule, so Home's 'After Next up' and 'Lately added' render at 17px regular, like prose, above 13px/600 'Who/Due' heads. Set `.cell-label {font:600 var(--t-label)/1.3 var(--sans); color:var(--label); margin:.75rem 0 .2rem}`. Move `.month-nav` into the module's `.tools-cell` as a second 44px bank ('Month' then '← Earlier', 'Later →'), so each page has one place for its controls. Give the screen `flex:1 1 100%`. (b) Status: 'The lights' sits in a 370px cell that is mostly empty, beside a half-width spend screen. Put the lamp key back in the module under 'Change the limit', as briefed, so the spend tube spans. (c) The month plate's '2 to come' contradicts Home's '5 coming'. Either count the same thing or say what it counts ('2 on these weeks').

FORM and SETTINGS should be one field system. (a) On idea_form, the rule `.idea-form .field > :not(label, legend, button.mic) {grid-column: 2 / 4}` makes Kind, Suggested by and Who it is for run into the mic column, while Title and Description stop at column 2. General still uses three-up boxes with 100-150px of dead space under short help, and the time-zone select wraps to 'Default (Vancouver · / UTC-07:00)'. Use one row per setting: a 13rem label column, the field at 28rem max, and help under it at 15px dim. General, AI model and Spending then read as the same register as the form and the Settings index.

TO DO register (/tasks). (a) The '#' column shows task ids in due order (4, 1, 2, 3), which reads as a scrambled index. Hide `.task-index .no`, or number the rows in display order. (b) `.row > details.edit > summary` has `height: var(--row)` and a bordered key face, so the four Edit keys stack into a touching column of boxes. Make it a ghost key: no fill or border at rest, the bone pencil and 'Edit', and the key face on row :hover or :focus-within with the lit edge; keep the 44px hit. (c) The head screen's `.bars` grid (auto-flow column, two rows) puts 'Late 2' beside 'Later 0' across the first line. Set it as one column in time order (Late, This week, Later, No date) at --t-tube-s, which fits within 9.5rem.

Keep 2px for contents lines only and set row leaders to `1px dotted color-mix(in srgb, var(--line-2) 75%, transparent)`. (b) Use one duration format: the Ideas screen says '2 h 45 min W' and the register says '2h 45 min W'. (c) Status, 'By kind of call': the table is squeezed to about 270px, so 'answering the / family' wraps and '6' and '1.26' float between its lines. Give `.tables` a min-width of about 22rem per table, or nowrap the 'What for' cell. (d) The non-breaking hyphen is missing in Status's 'Last call … gpt-6-luna' and in the 'Calls that ended oddly' rows.

TERMINAL scale, and PHONE pacing. name: Switchboard, Patched
tagline: Home is the map of the whole service, wired in each part's own colour: the terminal asks on its glass, its radar blips carry the day numerals that lead the Plans rows, setup is one service line, and the household pages run as contents lines along the foot.

firstDraft.name: Switchboard, Patched
firstDraft.concept: The videotex sommaire with four new features wired in. Every part's hairlines, leaders and figures take its own low-chroma colour in place of the 2px caps. Each plan row is led by its day numeral, and the same numeral labels its mark on the terminal's radar, so pointing at the row lights the mark. Setup is one service line, and the household's five pages run as contents lines in one strip along the foot. It should feel like a calm graphite switchboard. Only the terminal's glass, the lamps, Send and the Next up numeral give off phosphor light, and every other part is drawn in quiet coloured wiring.
